$comment: M2-17 — the `18` §8 determinism baseline over 10 000 seeded build permutations.

THIS TABLE IS SELF-GENERATED AND HAS NO EXTERNAL PUBLISHER. M0-06's Hash64 rows and M0-07's canonical-encoding rows were validated against EXTERNALLY PUBLISHED vectors — xxHash64's, and Landon Curt Noll's test_fnv.c — because xxHash64 and FNV-1a are published algorithms. There is no published authority for 'build permutation -> hash', so these rows were produced by the very resolver they guard.

WHAT IT THEREFORE PROVES: STABILITY. The `18` §8 pipeline is a pure function of its inputs, and its output cannot drift across a refactor or a compiler without a row here going red. That is exactly the accidental order-dependence `18` §11's parity line exists to catch. ACROSS A PLATFORM it proves nothing yet: .github/workflows/ci.yml's determinism job is 'if: false — gated: turns on with M5-12', so nothing runs this table on a second runtime today. The claim becomes true when that job does.

WHY IT IS NOT AN INDEPENDENT TRANSCRIPTION, WHICH IS THE BAR M2-15 MET. Rules/Combat/CombatLogReferenceVectors.json faced the same absence of a publisher — nobody publishes 'event list -> LogHash' vectors for this game — and still refused to generate from the code under test: its rows came from an independent Python transcription of `14` §16.6's encoding table and `05` §7's field list. That route was available there because the subject was a BYTE ENCODING: one table, transcribable in an afternoon. THE REASON IT WAS NOT TAKEN HERE IS COST, AND NOTHING MORE PRINCIPLED THAN COST. The subject is a ten-step resolution pipeline — collection from ten sources, a 23-function condition gate, five arithmetic steps in ordinal effect-id order, three kinds of cap override and per-step rounding — so a transcription would have to re-derive the whole of M2-02..M2-07's arithmetic, and would be roughly the size of the code it checks. That is a scope judgement M2-17 made and a later task may unmake; it is NOT a rule against second implementations. `18` §8's headnote is about divergence between SHIPPED implementations, and §11's parity line presupposes two — neither M0-06 nor M2-15 kept its generator, both ran a throwaway once and committed only the output, which is exactly what a Python transcription of §8 would be. So the provenance bar here is genuinely lower than M2-15's, and this paragraph exists to say so rather than to explain it away.

WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE: that the encoding or the resolution order is CORRECT. Correctness comes from M2-02..M2-07's per-op and per-step unit tests, which assert `18` §8's arithmetic against the document. A baseline generated from the code under test proves only self-consistency, and calling these 'reference vectors' in M0-06's sense would claim a validation that does not exist.

WHAT WAS CONFIRMED FIRST: before a single row below was written, CanonicalStateWriter was re-confirmed against FNV-1a's published vectors — Fnv1a64KnownAnswerTests and CanonicalStateWriterReferenceVectorTests, driven by Model/Snapshots/CanonicalStateWriterReferenceVectors.json. The hash function underneath these rows is externally validated even though the rows are not.

SUCCESSOR: real two-runtime parity is M5-12, on Linux x64 and Android ARM64 — the iOS ARM64 leg is authored but gated off with iOS itself (`16` D34). There is one resolver in one assembly today and no client build until M7, so `18` §11's 'client and server resolvers agree' has nothing to compare against yet. NOTE THE OBLIGATION IS NOT YET BOOKED: M5-12's tracker row names the LogHash table and the command-sequence parity test and does NOT name this one. M2-17 may not edit the tracker; the carry-forward was reported to the conductor instead, and until that row is amended nothing makes M5-12 pick this table up.

A FAILURE HERE IS A DETERMINISM BREAK, NEVER A TEST FIX. Regenerate only through the documented command in DslDeterminismBaselineWriter, and only after writing down why the hash moved. The writer stamps review.status = 'unreviewed'; this file's reader refuses that, so a regenerated table nobody reviewed stays red.

review.why: Fourth issue of the table, and the SECOND narrowing one — same mechanism as the third, a smaller cut. Making the board permanently visible (`16` D42) retired one op (REVEAL_TILES, which extended the tile preview range) and one stat (TILE_PREVIEW, the range it extended), because a board that is always wholly visible has no preview to widen and nothing to narrow one. `18` §11's op count moved 42 -> 41 and its §2.1 stat count 25 -> 24, so EffectVocabularyEmissionSets lost one row from each of two lists. BuildPermutationGenerator needed no change at all this time: neither token had a shaping arm, a valueScale argument or a fixture of its own — REVEAL_TILES was a RUN_AND_BOARD op the generator only ever emitted, and TILE_PREVIEW was an ordinary non-combat stat. EVERY CHUNK HASH BELOW MOVED, which `18` §11.1 documents: the generator anchors each axis by list[index % list.Count], so removing a token from any vocabulary shifts every subsequent permutation exactly as inserting one does. A regeneration, not a determinism break. 🔒 NO HASH WAS REGENERATED TO TURN A RED TEST GREEN, and the order of work is again what makes that checkable: the removal landed first across Core, the Application content set, the shipped curse catalogue and its schema; the whole solution built clean and EVERY OTHER TEST PROJECT WAS FULLY GREEN (Application 1 160, Client 491, Contract 160, Architecture 173, and the four asset suites) BEFORE this file was touched — the only red tests at regeneration time were this table's own five rows, and they were red because the emission set had legitimately shrunk. No behaviour of the `18` §8 pipeline changed: M2-02..M2-07's arithmetic is untouched, the retired op was a RUN_AND_BOARD op §8 never aggregated, and the retired stat was one of the non-combat stats §8 already skips from an actor's block. All twelve named rows kept their committed 'why' verbatim except one count inside 'non-combat-stat-skipped' (12 -> 10 non-combat stats, the same removal showing through in prose), and eleven of the twelve still name the same permutation. The twelfth is 'non-combat-stat-skipped' itself, 9 -> 14: each named row names the LOWEST-numbered build with its property, and taking a stat out of the non-combat list re-deals which build that is. Every_named_row_still_names_the_permutation_its_property_first_holds_at re-derives all twelve and would have gone red had any been written by hand. WHAT WAS NOT RE-REVIEWED: the $comment header's provenance argument is M2-17's and is unchanged — this table is still self-generated, still proves stability rather than correctness, and still rests underneath on FNV-1a's externally published vectors through CanonicalStateWriter, which Fnv1a64KnownAnswerTests and CanonicalStateWriterReferenceVectorTests confirmed green in the same assembly and the same run that wrote these rows.
